mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising the cost of capital and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers above 2% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage inflation and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation exceeds 3.5% during the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1.5% or more indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 1.5% or more over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the decline reverses within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 2% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% from the prior year indicates a weakening residential construction sector, which reduces demand for building materials and related equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST is more than 10% below prior-year level for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or housing starts rebound by more than 5% within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a contradictory signal indicating data inconsistency or measurement error, which historically has preceded short-term market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the data inconsistency is resolved within the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) of 5% or more signals reduced household buffer capacity, which increases reliance on credit and debt, raising default risk and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 65% of triggered episodes, or savings rebound above the prior year within two quarters.
